[printed at the TOP of page 339 as a separate, indented list item c) of 12.3.8.4 general rule 11); item b) ends at the foot of page 338 with "... the same externalized name as the externalized name of the function prototype; otherwise,"]
claim.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 14648 (inside the page-338 slice): "    b) if the externalized name of the function prototype is the externalized name of a function prototype definition specified in the same compilation group, the details are taken from that function prototype definition and the details in the external repository are ignored. The function that will be activated is the one with the same externalized name as the externalized name of the function prototype; otherwise, c) the details are taken from the external repository for the function with the same name as the externalized name of the function prototype. That function is the one that will be activated."  -- and the page-339 slice contains NO item c) at all (it opens directly at "12) Within the scope of the containing environment division ...").
claim.why_it_matters: General rule 11 (how the details for activating a function through a function prototype are obtained) is an ordered a)/b)/c) fallback chain. Item c) has been glued into the body of item b) with a literal "c)" left mid-sentence, so the terminal fallback rule is no longer a list item and cannot be cited as 12.3.8.4 GR 11 c). The immediately preceding general rule 10 (the program-prototype twin, lines 14638 and 14640) keeps its b) and c) as separate items, which proves the intended structure and that this is a transcription break, not an ISO layout choice.

verdict.reasoning: Tried to refute on all four grounds and could not. (1) Both sources quoted accurately. Rendered PDF p339 (printed 309) at 300 dpi: the page opens with a hanging-indented list item whose glyphs I read directly as a lowercase 'c' followed by a closing parenthesis -- 'c)' -- set at exactly the same left indent as items a) and b), followed by 'the details are taken from the external repository for the function with the same name as the externalized name of the function prototype. That function is the one that will be activated.' Rendered PDF p338 (printed 308) to fix the page break: GR 11 item b) is the last text on p338 and terminates at 'function prototype; otherwise,' with nothing after it. So the whole of item c) lives on p339 in the PDF. Markdown line 14648 is verbatim as quoted, ending '...; otherwise, c) the details are taken from ... will be activated.' -- one paragraph inside the page-338 slice, with a bare inline 'c)' mid-sentence. The page-339 slice (lines 14650-14661) has no item c); it opens at '12) Within the scope of the containing environment division'. (2) Not text loss -- every word of item c) is present, so this is not a 'missing text' defect. (3) Not mere page-break furniture or line wrapping. Two DISTINCT enumerated items were merged into one paragraph, which is a different kind of change from the collapsing of intra-paragraph line wraps that this transcription does everywhere. It also runs against the transcription's own page-break convention: eleven lines earlier, at line 14628, the continuation of GR 8 that spills onto p338 is placed AFTER the page-338 marker as its own paragraph, i.e. continuations follow the content forward onto the new page. Here the p339 item was instead pulled backwards into the previous page's slice. (4) It changes structure, and with it citability. The load-bearing control is the sibling rule: GR 10 is the program-prototype twin of GR 11, word-for-word parallel, and its b) and c) survive as separate items at lines 14638 and 14640 with the same four-space indent. That asymmetry between two identically-structured rules is only explicable as a transcription break at the page boundary. Consequence: in the markdown, 12.3.8.4 GR 11 has only items a) and b), so the terminal fallback of the resolution chain cannot be cited as GR 11 c) and is attributed to the wrong page for any page-anchored citation; it also reads as though b) contains its own alternative. Verified section numbering: 12.3.8.4 General rules at line 14599, GR 11 at line 14642. Confirmed real.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed; two refinements. (a) No text is lost -- the defect is purely the loss of the list-item boundary plus misattribution to the wrong page slice, so it is structural/citational rather than semantic: a reader can still recover the fallback chain from the run-on sentence, but 12.3.8.4 GR 11 c) is no longer an addressable item and now sits in the page-338 slice although the PDF prints it entirely on page 339. (b) The claim's supporting argument is stronger than stated: besides GR 10 retaining separate b)/c) at lines 14638/14640, line 14628 shows this transcription's normal page-break handling is to carry spilled text FORWARD into the new page's slice (GR 8's continuation onto page 338), whereas here the page-339 item was pulled BACKWARD into the page-338 slice -- an anomaly in the opposite direction from the convention. Repair: split line 14648 after 'function prototype; otherwise,' and move 'c) the details are taken from the external repository for the function with the same name as the externalized name of the function prototype. That function is the one that will be activated.' into the page-339 slice as a four-space-indented list item ahead of item 12), mirroring lines 14638/14640.
